issues.item: Threat in Movements: Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
issues.explanation: The threat items imply a trauma context dominated by interpersonal assault or ambush cues (others' sudden movements, ominous silence) rather than toxic chemical exposure. For a chemical exposure trauma, these are hard to reconcile unless there is additional unreported assault/combat context.

issues.item: Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
issues.explanation: The negative appraisal about losing connection to community/culture is not well anchored to the rest of the profile. The other selected items center on intrusive memory, overwhelm, and coping incapacity, but there are no related triggers, memories, or strategies suggesting social/cultural disconnection as a core post-trauma theme.

issues.item: Lost Community: I have lost my connection to my community and culture
issues.explanation: This item is the least coherent with the rest of the profile. For a 72-year-old married male Coast Guard patient with toxic chemical exposure, the dominant pattern elsewhere is threat, intrusive sensory memory, and low coping around reminders. 'Lost connection to my community and culture' is not impossible, but it is not well supported by the trauma type or by the other selected threat/memory/appraisal items, which center on danger, overwhelm, and inability to handle recall. It reads as a broader social-identity consequence that is disconnected from the active formulation, where Memory and Threat are tightly linked and Negative Appraisals are threat-focused. This makes that individual appraisal item clinically weakly matched to the rest of the self-report.

vignette: Kofi had always taken pride in his decades-long service in the Coast Guard, but it was a single incident involving toxic chemical exposure that changed everything. He remembered the day vividly - the smell of the chemicals, the sound of his colleagues' panicked voices, and the feeling of helplessness as he watched the scene unfold. Even now, when Kofi closes his eyes, the memory replays like a film in his mind, each frame seared into his brain with photographic precision. As time passed, Kofi began to notice that unusual silence made him feel on edge. He would find himself scanning the room, waiting for something to happen, even in the safety of his own home. His wife, Akua, would try to reassure him, but Kofi couldn't shake off the feeling that danger lurked around every corner. This sense of threat was constantly fueled by memories of the chemical exposure, which seemed to replay on a loop in his mind. When these memories surfaced, Kofi felt overwhelmed by emotion, and he would have to stop whatever he was doing to collect himself. Kofi had come to believe that he couldn't deal with even the slightest upset. He thought that if he allowed himself to think about the event, he wouldn't be able to handle it, and this fear of being overwhelmed led him to avoid thinking about it altogether. However, this avoidance only seemed to reinforce his conviction that the world was a dangerous place, and that he needed to be constantly on guard. This sense of threat, in turn, made Kofi more prone to strong physical reactions when something reminded him of the stressful experience. As Kofi's symptoms worsened, he found it increasingly difficult to navigate his daily routine. He would become easily startled by sudden noises, and even the sight of certain chemicals or equipment would trigger a strong reaction. His wife began to notice the changes in him, and she encouraged him to seek help. But Kofi was hesitant, convinced that he couldn't cope with the emotions that therapy might stir up. Despite his reservations, Kofi's worsening symptoms eventually led him to seek professional help. He is now struggling to come to terms with the fact that his traumatic experience has left an indelible mark on his life. As he begins this new chapter, Kofi is most afraid of losing control and being overwhelmed by his emotions. But he also hopes that therapy will help him find a way to quiet the constant threat alerts in his mind, and learn to navigate the world with a sense of safety and security once again.
